prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth strip supports a coarse front-to-back layout: across the five frames, nearby people and foreground fixtures are bright while the rear walls, doorway, cabinets, and corridor are darker; approximate distances are about 0.5–1.5 m for the nearest people or counter edges and roughly 2–5 m for background surfaces. In frame 1, a person left-of-centre is about 1–2 m ahead, with a bright foreground object at lower centre-right closer than 1 m; in frames 2–3, people and counter/table surfaces occupy the near field, while in frames 4–5 a woman remains about 1–2 m in front as the view turns into the corridor. The sequence indicates camera rotation to the right more strongly than simple approach or retreat, with foreground objects sweeping laterally and the final person moving from centre-right toward centre while remaining at a similar range. Depth makes distance ordering and silhouettes clearer than RGB, including foreground occlusion of farther furniture, but absolute metre estimates are uncertain and several dark or blurred regions, thin structures, and body boundaries have implausibly flat or merged depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies people in every frame and labels several scene objects—refrigerator, TV, chair, dining table, and a small bowl—making object extents and overlaps clearer than in RGB. In frame 1, one person is left-of-centre about 1–2 m away and partly cropped above, while the refrigerator lies behind and to that person's left; frames 2–3 contain overlapping people roughly 0.5–2 m ahead, with one central person occluding another and nearby furniture below or to the right. Frames 4–5 show a single dominant person approximately 1–2 m ahead, first near centre and then right-of-centre, with small duplicate person fragments marking partially visible or overlapping body regions; the shifting masks reflect the camera turning right. This map is unreliable for metric distance and facing direction, and its duplicated person labels, missed counters and walls, fragmented masks, and inconsistent colours indicate detection or instance-assignment errors.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides articulated spatial cues that RGB and the other maps do not: frame 1 shows a mostly full body left-of-centre, with the head and upper torso near the top and the legs extending downward, while frames 2–3 contain only small hand or partial-limb detections near the centre because bodies are close, cropped, or occluded. In frames 4–5, facial keypoints and a horizontal shoulder line place a person about 1–2 m in front; the face remains oriented broadly toward the camera wearer as the camera turns and the person shifts from centre-right to farther right in the panorama. The frame-1 person is farther left and appears side-on rather than squarely facing the camera, while the visible hand detections in the middle frames are likely within roughly 0.5–1 m of the wearer and therefore near arm's reach. Pose helps reveal body orientation, joint placement, and which body parts are visible or occluded, but the missing torsos and limbs, floating hand skeletons, sparse facial points, and absent detections for some segmented people make reach, gaze, and inter-person distance highly uncertain.
